analysis:
All three changed files are documentation: changelog.d/m5-paged-automatic-concurrency.md, docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (new 'Serving width by chip' section at head lines 369-381) and docs/architecture/inference.md (patch hunk @@ -97,9 +97,14). Together they describe a Swift behavior change that is not in this batch: on M5 Pro/Max/Ultra, paged-auto models default to engine width 8 instead of 4 when engine_v2_max_concurrent is absent. The width falls back to the configured width under Low Power Mode or thermal pressure. The docs say KV grants, load quotation and activation reserve are unchanged, and that the coordinator's per-model quality cap and fixed-workspace memory concurrency still bound admission.

Security-relevant observations for later passes. Chip identity comes from the machdep.cpu.brand_string sysctl, which is self-reported by the provider and not attested. The effect is limited to local concurrency, so it is not a trust decision. The change touches the T-041 surface (prefix cache and timing oracle) and T-028 (residual GPU memory) only indirectly, because higher concurrency means more co-resident tenant requests per slot. Process-level memory admission via ProcessMemoryLedger/AdmissionV2 is documented as unchanged. Any Swift source change (ServingPerformanceProfiles.automaticConcurrency, EngineV2Bridge.hasPostureGatedWidth) would need to confirm that width 8 is bounded by the same memory admission and that the posture fallback is fail-safe.

This batch has no changes to authorization, attestation, encryption, wire protocol or billing. The docs-only text introduces no new code attack surface and no contradiction with the threat-model assumptions.
